suppressions.reason: The request body is the reranking test's prompt, built from the queries and documents in fixtures/ (committed in this repository), and it goes to the Ollama server the operator configures (OLLAMA_HOST in .env): sending that text to the model under test is the benchmark. No secret, user upload or other file reaches it. The app runs on the operator's machine, listening on 127.0.0.1.

Writing the download is this script's job: pnpm datasets:fetch saves the public benchmark files pinned in fixtures/*/manifest.json (committed in this repository: fixed Hugging Face revisions and GitHub commits) under .data/datasets/, through a .part file renamed when complete. The files are test data, read by the benchmarks; the script never executes them. It runs only by hand on a developer machine.

The package and repository names come from the web-search cases in fixtures/web-search/cases/*.json, committed in this repository, never from a user or a model; the request reads their public latest version from api.github.com (releases/latest) to score the answer, so the only file data that leaves the machine is those public names. The test runs only from the CLI (pnpm bench) on a developer machine.

The test runs only from the CLI (pnpm bench) on a developer machine.

The URL is built from fixtures/*/manifest.json, committed in this repository (public dataset or repository name and pinned revision or commit), so the only file data in the request is those public identifiers, sent to huggingface.co or codeload.github.com. pnpm datasets:fetch runs only by hand on a developer machine.

The HTML comes from mammoth converting .data/files/17incddocguide.docx, a public IRS document committed in this repository, never user input; the stripped cell text only feeds a Markdown table whose cell() escapes every < and > before writing fixtures/doc-to-markdown/reference/, so no tag can reach the output. The script is a maintainer tool run by hand on a developer machine. A follow-up replace removing stray < and > (output identical) did not clear the alert, so it is not worth a code change.

musl CVE-2026-107891 is fixed in 1.2.6-r6, not yet in Alpine 3.24: `apk policy musl` on node:24-alpine (Alpine 3.24.4) on 2026-11-28 offers only 1.2.6-r3, which the image has after `apk upgrade`. Picked up by the next build (docker build --pull, which pnpm security --build and the docker:build task run). The image runs only locally, its port published on 127.0.0.1.
